drawdown_context.control_note: Stayed in S&P 600; +178.3% forward return is the strongest single positive in the survivorship cohort and the highest-stakes false-positive risk for a short-bias forensic framework.

rfm_tuples.R: Filing discloses 'Our backlog as of December 31, 2024 was $7.7 billion.' MD&A says revenue decline was 'driven by ... the lower quantity of new business wins prior to the Spin, along with the slower backlog burn rate and the mix of mature and longer duration studies in our portfolio.' No explicit book-to-bill ratio, no quarterly net awards table, no cancellation-rate disclosure.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm backlog number and management's stated drivers of revenue decline. Mode B: CRO industry-standard KPI is net book-to-bill (typically reported >1.0x as bookings/revenue) — derive whether the filing's CHOICE to disclose only ending backlog (a stock) without the flow (net awards, cancellations) is itself a Mode B omission.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Backlog $7.7B vs LTM revenue $2.696B = 2.86x revenue (consistent with industry norm of 2.5-3.0x). HONEST disclosure that 'lower quantity of new business wins prior to the Spin' drove deceleration — management is admitting the post-spin sales motion underperformed for ~18 months. NOT disclosed: explicit book-to-bill ratio, net awards by quarter, gross cancellations. ICON/IQV/MEDP all report net book-to-bill ratios; absence here is informative but not deceptive given backlog level is candidly stated. Note the filing explicitly warns 'our backlog might not be indicative of our future revenues' and 'we might not realize all of the anticipated future revenue reflected in our backlog' — appropriately humble framing.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B partial finding — the absence of book-to-bill is a peer-relative disclosure gap, but the filing's candor about 'lower quantity of new business wins prior to the Spin' is the kind of bad-news admission that an honesty-alpha framework should REWARD, not punish. A liar would hide the demand-side weakness; FTRE names it directly.

rfm_tuples.R: 'For the year ended December 31, 2024, our top ten customers based on revenue accounted for approximately 53% of our consolidated revenue and our top ten customers based on backlog accounted for approximately 51% of our total backlog. For the year ended December 31, 2024, two customers accounted for approximately 14.3% and 10.5% of revenue.' Two customers also 17.0% and 11.2% of gross A/R + unbilled services.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: pull concentration numbers. Mode B: derive (i) trajectory of concentration vs prior year; (ii) whether A/R concentration > revenue concentration implies stretched payment terms with the largest sponsor.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Top-2 customer concentration WORSENED slightly YoY: 2024 14.3%+10.5% = 24.8% vs 2023 11.6%+11.4% = 23.0% of revenue. A/R concentration (17.0%+11.2% = 28.2%) exceeds revenue concentration (24.8%) — top sponsors are paying slower or have larger unbilled balances. With pharma R&D outsourcing facing biotech-funding pressure, a CRO with ~25% revenue in two sponsors is exposed to single-sponsor program cuts. HONESTLY disclosed (full table provided).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Concentration is real and trending wrong way, but disclosed cleanly. Not a deception signal; an operational risk signal.

rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: pull margin walk. Mode B: derive whether the magnitude/direction is consistent with management's framing of a normal post-spin standalone-cost ramp, or whether it implies structural margin impairment.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Two-year operating-income walk: +$187.1M (2022, inside Labcorp) -> +$32.0M (2023, 6 months standalone) -> ($161.9M) (2024, first full standalone year). That is a $349M GAAP operating swing in two years. Direct-cost ratio expanded 570bps (74.5% -> 80.2%); SG&A +25% YoY on -5% revenue. Some of this is standalone-cost ramp (Transition Services Agreement winding down, IT/finance/HR standup) and is acknowledged by management. But SBC nearly doubled ($25.4M 2022 -> $42.7M 2023 -> $58.4M 2024) and restructuring charges $50.1M (2024) vs $21.2M (2023). The combination of revenue down, costs up, and interest expense ~18x 2022 level is a textbook 'broken spinoff Year 1' P&L.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The OPERATING reality is severe distress. But all of it is disclosed transparently — three-year side-by-side income statement, explicit reconciliations, no smoothing. This is the canonical case where the honesty-alpha framework should distinguish 'bad business honestly reported' (which the market can already price) from 'bad business deceptively reported' (which is the alpha). FTRE is the former.

rfm_tuples.R: Note 23 Subsequent Events + Item 9B: 'On February 28, 2025, the Company entered into an amendment (the "Second Credit Amendment") to modify a financial covenant ... increased the Company's maximum quarterly Total Leverage Ratio (as defined in the Existing Credit Agreement) from 5.30:1.00 to 6.00:1.00 for the fiscal quarters ending on September 30, 2025 through ... reverting to 5.30:1.00 thereafter. In consideration ... the Company paid a fee to consenting lenders and has agreed during the covenant adjustment period to certain additional limitations with respect to investments, restricted payments and liens.' This is the SECOND covenant amendment in 9 months (first on May 3, 2024).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: detect covenant amendment / relief. Mode B: derive what management's adjusted-EBITDA forecast must look like for max leverage to threaten the prior 5.30x cap — i.e. back-solve management's implied bad-case forecast.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Total debt $1,142M / implied adj. EBITDA at 5.30x covenant = $215.5M required. New 6.00x cap = $190.3M required. The 70bps covenant cushion grant implies management/lenders anticipate adj. EBITDA could fall to roughly $190-215M range in 2025-2026 — i.e. a >30% decline from the unstated 2024 base. This is a DISTRESS signal: two covenant amendments in 9 months, with restrictions on investments/restricted payments/liens added as consideration. Bond indenture also has asset-sale covenant requiring net proceeds to redeem notes (Endpoint sale already triggered $76M current portion).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Highest-discrimination single distress signal in the filing. Two covenant amendments in 9 months with leverage cap raised from 5.30 to 6.00 = textbook 'covenant ratchet' that precedes either operational turnaround or restructuring. Honestly disclosed (it's a same-day subsequent event in Item 9B), but the signal itself is bearish on a forward 12-month view.

rfm_tuples.R: Goodwill $1,710.4M (2024) vs $1,739.4M (2023). 'The Company assesses goodwill for impairment at least annually... Although the Company believes that the current assumptions and estimates used in its goodwill analysis are reasonable, supportable, and appropriate, continued efforts to maintain or improve the performance of these businesses could be impacted... primarily delays or lower demand resulting in lower contract bookings and the related delay or reduction in revenue, increases in customer termination activity or increases in operating costs.' Goodwill+intangibles = $2,366M vs total stockholders' equity (implied from balance sheet) much smaller than this, and operating loss of $161.9M in 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: detect goodwill cushion language. Mode B: derive impairment probability given negative operating income, covenant ratchet, and management's own cushion language.
rfm_tuples.M_value: $1.71B goodwill against operating LOSS of $161.9M in 2024 is a goodwill-impairment 'when, not if' situation under quantitative ASC 350. Management did NOT take an impairment in 2024 (cushion still 'substantially exceeded' book value per filing language), but the same paragraph names three triggers — lower bookings, terminations, higher opex — and FTRE is currently experiencing all three. Single-segment reporter means the test is at the entire-company level, making a partial impairment more likely than a full write-off. If the FY25 enterprise value implied by debt+equity stays where it sat ~cutoff (debt $1.14B + market-cap ~$0.5-0.7B), the implied EV is below the carrying amount of net assets including goodwill — quantitative trigger.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honest disclosure of the risk in the right place (critical accounting estimates) with the right hedges. The risk is real but not hidden; it is exactly the kind of pre-announced impairment that markets can price.

rfm_tuples.R: '/s/ Deloitte & Touche LLP Raleigh, North Carolina March 3, 2025 We have served as the Company's auditor since 2022.'
rfm_tuples.f: auditor_change_tracker — verify Big 4 audit, tenure, ICFR opinion, any disagreements.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Deloitte & Touche, Big 4, since 2022 (3 years — full tenure of the spinoff company; appointed pre-spin). Clean ICFR attestation issued for the first time this year (newly required as accelerated filer). Critical audit matter is revenue recognition on long-duration fixed-price contracts (industry-standard CAM, not a fraud red flag). No 8-K Item 4.01 events. No disagreements. AUDITOR SIGNAL: CLEAN.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Auditor signal is clean. Important PASS — the framework cannot attribute the operating distress to an audit/accounting deception signal.

rfm_tuples.R: 'As reported in our Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024 ... management identified material weaknesses in our internal controls over financial reporting that existed because the company did not have sufficient resources which in turn led to an inability to effectively perform certain control activities... During the fourth quarter of 2024, the Company successfully completed the testing and evaluation necessary to conclude that, as of December 31, 2024, the previously identified material weaknesses have been remediated.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: detect material weakness language. Mode B: derive whether remediation claim is credible given (a) timing (Q4 2024 close), (b) prior weakness was 'insufficient resources' — a recurring risk in a thinly-staffed standalone, (c) related immaterial restatement of prior periods.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Two-related-prior-issues admitted: (1) material weakness identified in Q1 2024 10-Q (May 24, 2024 filing), remediated by year-end 2024; (2) immaterial restatement of prior period financial statements (goodwill impairment carrying-value error, revenue understatement from customer matter, expense accrual understatement, depreciation understatement) — concluded immaterial under ASC 250 but corrected. Both are spin-related accounting hangover issues, both fully disclosed, both with full audit committee process. Deloitte issued clean ICFR opinion on Dec 31, 2024 controls. NOT a clean-history company, but the disclosure is candid and the remediation appears genuine.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Yellow flag, not red. Material weakness remediated within ~7 months is fast but plausible; immaterial restatement disclosed in proper place. A deception case would hide these or call them 'reclassifications'; FTRE labels them explicitly.

rfm_tuples.R: No going-concern language in filing. 'Our debt and debt covenant requirements may limit cash flow available to invest in the ongoing needs of our business' is a generic risk factor, not a 12-month substantial-doubt warning. Cash $118.5M (2024) vs $108.6M (2023). Operating cash flow $262.8M (2024, helped by $309.9M A/R decrease — likely Endpoint sale collections + working capital release).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: going_concern_detector. Mode B: derive whether the operating cash flow is sustainable or working-capital-driven.
rfm_tuples.M_value: going_concern_local: NO_GOING_CONCERN, 0 substantial-doubt matches. Liquidity: $118.5M cash + $450M undrawn revolver = $568M of available liquidity vs $74.8M current portion of long-term debt. Operating CF $262.8M but $309.9M of that came from A/R decrease (collection acceleration + Endpoint sale) — underlying cash generation is much weaker. Term loan B paid down $412.5M (helped by $276.6M Endpoint proceeds). PASS on explicit claim. 7.5% senior notes don't mature until 2030; term loans 2028/2030.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: No going-concern issue and the company has 3+ years of debt runway. The operating distress is real but not a near-term solvency event. Important PASS — framework correctly does NOT trigger going-concern detector.

rfm_tuples.R: 'We entered into a Cooperation Agreement, dated February 21, 2025 (the "Cooperation Agreement"), with Starboard Value LP ("Starboard"), an activist investor ... regarding certain changes to the composition of our board, including the appointment of an independent director, Erin Russell, and an option for Starboard to appoint an additional Starboard employee to our board.' Plus extensive 'Actions of activist stockholders' risk factor.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: extract activist event. Mode B: this is the KEY false-positive-risk question — when a CRO with strong backlog, stable cash, and clean accounting is taken up by Starboard, what is the forward-12mo distribution of outcomes (sale, breakup, management change, operational turnaround) vs further deterioration?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Starboard cooperation agreement signed 10 days before the 10-K filing (Feb 21, 2025 — pre-cutoff). Two board changes negotiated. Starboard's CRO/healthcare-services playbook is typically: (a) push for sale/strategic-alternatives review, (b) cost-cut + margin reset, (c) management/board overhaul. Combined with FTRE's profile (single-segment, $7.7B backlog, depressed valuation post-spinoff distress, comparable-company multiples on healthy CROs like ICON/IQV/MEDP imply substantial upside under any margin normalization), the activist catalyst is structurally bullish. This is precisely the kind of post-cutoff CATALYST that a short-bias forensic framework can miss because it isn't a 'lie' in the 10-K.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Strongest single Mode B finding for the NO-SHORT case. Starboard's involvement materially changes the forward distribution. The honesty-alpha framework should DOWN-WEIGHT short conviction when a credible activist (Starboard has CRO-adjacent priors) is already engaged at the cutoff date with cooperation agreement signed.

rfm_tuples.R: Spin completed June 30, 2023; FY24 is first full-year standalone. MD&A attributes revenue decline to 'lower quantity of new business wins prior to the Spin' and 'slower backlog burn rate'. Risk factors include extensive 'Risks Relating to Our Spin from Labcorp' section: indemnification, TSA wind-down, IT systems standup, accounting controls.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B claim_evolution: did the FY24 10-K materially change the narrative vs the FY23 10-K? Are spin-related transition costs flagged as 'one-time' or 'ongoing'? Is management blaming the past (pre-spin sales) or owning the future (post-spin pipeline)?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Management's 2024 narrative ATTRIBUTES the revenue weakness to PRE-SPIN sales execution ('lower quantity of new business wins prior to the Spin') and to portfolio MIX ('mature and longer duration studies') — both of which are diagnoses with finite-life implications (new sales motion can be rebuilt; portfolio churns over 3-5 years). This is materially DIFFERENT from a 'demand is shrinking' narrative — and the $7.7B backlog supports the diagnosis (backlog/revenue 2.86x is healthy). Restructuring charges $50.1M (2024) and SG&A +25% reflect active reorganization. The Spin transition costs are flagged as TSA-related and winding down — appropriately bounded.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The claim evolution is CONSISTENT WITH A HONEST TURNAROUND THESIS, not with a deception. Management owns the bad results, attributes them to specific identifiable causes (pre-spin sales gap + study-mix transition + standalone cost ramp), and is taking action (restructuring, divestiture of non-core Endpoint, debt paydown, covenant relief, activist board reset). This is the textbook 'honestly disclosed bad year for a fixable business' setup that DRIVES the post-cutoff rally.

supplemental_signals.auditor_signal: CLEAN_AUDITOR_TENURE (Deloitte & Touche, since 2022, Big 4, clean ICFR)
supplemental_signals.material_weakness_history: Q1 2024 material weakness ('insufficient resources') REMEDIATED by Dec 31, 2024; Deloitte clean ICFR opinion. Plus immaterial restatement of prior periods for goodwill carrying-value error, revenue understatement, expense accrual & depreciation errors.
supplemental_signals.balance_sheet_health: Cash $118.5M + $450M undrawn revolver; debt $1,142M (7.5% notes due 2030 $570M; term A 2028 $417.3M; term B 2030 $154.7M). Term loan B paid down $412.5M in 2024 using Endpoint proceeds. Covenant amendments May 2024 and Feb 2025 (max leverage 5.30 -> 6.00).
supplemental_signals.operating_metric_trajectory: Revenue $2,696M (-5.1% YoY); operating income $(161.9M) vs +$32.0M vs +$187.1M (2024/23/22); backlog $7.7B (2.86x revenue); top-2 customers 14.3%+10.5%=24.8% of revenue (worsened from 23.0%).
supplemental_signals.spinoff_context: Spun from Labcorp Jun 30, 2023; first full year standalone; TSA winding down; Endpoint Clinical / Patient Access (Enabling Services Segment) divested to Arsenal Capital Partners for $340M in Q2 2024, $276.6M net proceeds.
supplemental_signals.activist_catalyst: Starboard Value LP Cooperation Agreement dated Feb 21, 2025 (pre-cutoff). Two board seats (Erin Russell + optional Starboard employee). CRO-sector activist with M&A/breakup playbook. STRUCTURALLY BULLISH catalyst that explains the +178% forward return.
supplemental_signals.ceo_status: Thomas Pike — President/CEO/Chairman; tenure since spin (no leadership change). Compensation Sept 2024 RSU amendment indicates continued engagement.
supplemental_signals.insider_signal_derived: No filed Form 4 distress patterns detected from 10-K text; key insider event is COMPANY-LEVEL Starboard cooperation, not individual insider de-risking.
supplemental_signals.covenant_relief_signal: Two amendments in 9 months; max leverage ratchet 5.30 -> 6.00 implies management/lender bad-case adj. EBITDA range $190-215M (down >30% from 2024 base). Investment/restricted-payment/lien restrictions added as consideration.
supplemental_signals.goodwill_impairment_setup: $1.71B goodwill against operating LOSS $161.9M; single-segment test; FY24 cushion 'substantially exceeded' book value but all three triggers (lower bookings, terminations, higher opex) currently active; impairment risk in FY25 is high but already partly priced.

summary: FTRE is the canonical CONTROL_SURVIVOR test for the honesty-alpha framework: a CRO with severe operational distress (revenue -5.1%, operating loss $161.9M, two covenant amendments in 9 months ratcheting max leverage from 5.30x to 6.00x, $1.71B goodwill against negative operating income, prior material weakness, immaterial restatement, top-2 customer concentration 25%) that nonetheless rallied +178% post-cutoff. The framework correctly identifies the distress — but EVERY signal is disclosed transparently in the filing: Deloitte clean ICFR; explicit covenant amendment in Item 9B same day as filing; full three-year income statement with no smoothing; goodwill-impairment triggers named in critical accounting estimates; material weakness disclosed and remediation walked through. The decisive Mode B finding is C9 — Starboard Value LP Cooperation Agreement dated Feb 21, 2025 (10 days before the 10-K), giving Starboard 1-2 board seats. Combined with (a) $7.7B backlog at 2.86x revenue (healthy), (b) management's diagnosis that revenue weakness stems from PRE-SPIN sales execution + portfolio mix (both fixable), (c) $568M available liquidity with no near-term debt maturities, (d) Endpoint divestiture already done and proceeds used to retire term loan B, the activist catalyst transformed a depressed-multiple distressed-spinoff into a credible turnaround/strategic-alternatives trade. The framework should score this as MODERATE distress with HIGH OFFSETTING CATALYST, producing a composite that does NOT cross any short-trigger threshold. This is exactly the SRPT-style 'honestly bad business' case the honesty-alpha thesis says to EXCLUDE from shorts even when individual forensic detectors fire.
